title: Ukraine History Tracker Update — Mon May 18, 2026
summary: Russia fired 524 Shahed-type drones and 22 missiles (including 14 ballistic) at Ukraine overnight into May 18, 2026 — one of its most intense barrages of the month. Ukraine's Air Force intercepted 503 drones and 4 missiles, but 16 drones and 18 missiles scored direct hits at 34 locations. Odesa bore the worst damage: residential buildings in two districts, a kindergarten, a lyceum, and a police station were struck, injuring 20 people including two children. On the front lines, 195 combat engagements were recorded on Day 1,544, with Pokrovsk and Hulyaipole as the hottest sectors; Ukraine's Military Intelligence (HUR) claimed full control of Stepnohirsk in Zaporizhzhia Oblast. Russian cumulative military losses reached an estimated 1,350,010 personnel since February 24, 2022, with 1,220 additional casualties in the past 24 hours.

title: Ukraine History Tracker Update — Sun May 17, 2026
summary: Ukraine launched its largest-ever drone attack on Russia overnight into May 17 — approximately 556 drones targeting Moscow's oil refinery, Transneft pumping stations, and the ELMA Technopark, with debris striking Sheremetyevo Airport and causing ~200 flight cancellations. At least 4 people were killed in Russia and 12 wounded. Zelensky called the strike 'entirely justified.' Simultaneously, Russia fired 287 drones at Ukraine (279 intercepted), injuring 9 in Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia. On the front lines, 234 combat engagements were recorded with the Pokrovsk sector most active; Ukrainian forces advanced in the Hulyaipole direction. Russian cumulative military losses reached ~1,348,790 on Day 1,543 of the full-scale invasion.

title: Ukraine History Tracker Update — Thu May 15, 2026
summary: Russia unleashed the most massive aerial barrage of the war on May 13–14: 1,428 Shahed drones (single-day record), 50+ missiles, and 302 guided aerial bombs demolishing a Kyiv apartment building and killing 24 civilians including 3 children — Day 1,541 of the invasion. Zelensky accused Russia of timing the attack to Trump's China state visit. Ukraine struck back overnight, setting Rosneft's Ryazan refinery ablaze (~180 km from Moscow), destroying military aircraft at Yeysk, and hitting air defense systems in Luhansk and Crimea. Russia and Ukraine completed a 205-for-205 POW exchange. Finland's Helsinki airport closed 3 hours after suspected Russian drone overflight tested the NATO Baltic flank. Frontline combat surged to 257 engagements on May 15; Russia's estimated military casualties reached ~1,346,500. Russian energy losses from Ukraine's 2026 drone campaign now exceed $8B.

title: Ukraine History Tracker Update — Wed May 13, 2026
summary: Russia launched a large-scale combined phased strike on May 13 — an initial Shahed wave to overload air defenses followed by cruise and ballistic missiles targeting energy infrastructure and government buildings across eight regions. At least 8 civilians were killed and 11 injured in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast alone, with additional casualties in Lutsk, Rivne, Kharkiv, Odesa, Cherkasy, Kryvyi Rih, and Poltava. Ukraine's STING Drone Hunters intercepted 100+ drones. Overnight, Ukrainian long-range strike drones hit Russia's Astrakhan gas processing plant near the Caspian Sea despite Russia's claimed shootdown of 286 Ukrainian drones — extending Ukraine's deep-strike energy campaign to its farthest southern reach. Russia's estimated military personnel losses reached approximately 1,344,290, and Day 1,539 of the full-scale invasion was the most intense bombardment since the ceasefire collapse.

title: Ukraine History Tracker Update — Tue May 12, 2026
summary: Hours after the US-brokered Victory Day ceasefire (May 9–11) expired, Russia launched 216 Shahed drones at Ukraine — 192 were intercepted but at least 1 person was killed and 6 injured. In Kyiv, drone debris struck a 16-storey residential building in the Obolon district. President Zelensky declared: 'Russia itself chose to end the partial silence.' Ukraine's Foreign Minister Sybiha confirmed Ukraine had proposed a ceasefire extension; Moscow refused and escalated. The Kremlin simultaneously stated there are no 'specifics' on ending the war, collapsing any diplomatic momentum from the truce. The 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner exchange promised under the ceasefire remains unexecuted. Russia's estimated personnel losses reached approximately 1,343,160 since Feb. 24, 2022 — Day 1,538 of the full-scale invasion. Events, map-lines, KPIs, political, and meta updated.

title: Ukraine History Tracker Update — Mon May 11, 2026
summary: The US-brokered three-day ceasefire (May 9–11) expired on May 11 with no extension announced. Russian attacks on the final day killed 3 civilians and wounded 16 across Ukraine: 2 killed in Kherson Oblast (12 settlements struck), 1 killed in Zaporizhzhia, with 5 wounded in Kharkiv, 4 in Donetsk, and 3 in Mykolaiv. One Iskander-M ballistic missile was fired from occupied Crimea; 180 front-line combat clashes were recorded. ISW assessed Russia used the ceasefire window for troop rotations and logistics resupply. The 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner exchange remains unexecuted. Peace talks are deadlocked over Russia's demand that Ukraine withdraw from Donetsk. Russia's total personnel losses reached an estimated 1,342,030 since Feb. 24, 2022 — Day 1,537 of the full-scale invasion. Events, map-lines, KPIs, and meta updated.

Ukraine's Air Force intercepted all 27 overnight drones. Russia also stalled the landmark 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner exchange, with Putin claiming Ukraine was 'not ready'; Ukraine said Moscow was breaking a pledge made to the United States. Day 1,536 of the full-scale invasion. Events, map-lines, KPIs, political, and meta updated.
